title: Permission shadowing, canary rollback signals, and customer opt-in migration plan for RBAC v2
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: introduce a lightweight 'permission shadowing' mode that writes RBAC v2 state in parallel but does not change enforcement for a customer cohort, instrument fine-grained observability probes for divergence and regression detection, and define canary rollback signals and a customer opt-in/off window for safe cutover. This ticket coordinates engineering work (dual-write, backfill throttling, reconciliation sampler), observability (telemetry, dashboards, alert thresholds), and customer-facing opt-in UX and comms.
acceptance_criteria: Dual-write enabled for 5% canary cohort with shadow enforcement only
Divergence sampler deployed that flags >0.1% permission mismatches per 24h for canary
End-to-end test harness that replays 50 representative API flows against v1 and v2 and asserts functional parity
Rollback automation that disables v2 enforcement and re-routes reads to v1 within 3 minutes and verifies successful state re-sync
Customer opt-in toggle in Console with audit trail and email template for comms
tasks: Implement permission-shadow flag and dual-write plumbing (auth-service & role-store)
Add per-request tagging (rbac-v2-shadow=true) for sampling and metrics
Build reconciliation sampler job and dashboard (grafana panel + alert)
Create canary cohort selector and rollout controller (region, org size filters)
Integrate audit-log hooks to capture v1 vs v2 decision context in S3/Pulsar
Implement rollback playbook and CLI automation (ops-runbook)
Prepare customer opt-in Console flow and consent logging
Coordinate security review and threat model updates
technical_notes: Shadowing approach: write canonical grant/deny records to v2 store and annotate requests; enforcement remains on v1 unless opt-in flag present
Backfill throttling: use token-bucket per-org with adaptive slow-start to avoid cache stampedes; default 50 orgs/minute configurable per release wave
Reconciliation: deterministic diff algorithm based on (principal, resource, action, grant_id); tolerates eventual order differences by using tombstones for deletes
SSO mapping: user/group IDs must be normalized via canonical SAML NameID mapping layer to avoid mismatches; mapping verification job included
Audit logs: each decision must include trace_id, policy_version, principal_hash (pseudonymized), and decision_source (v1|v2|shadow)
risks: Permission divergence causing accidental escalation if shadowing accidentally flips to enforcement
Backfill-induced DB throttling on peak churn orgs
SAML name-mismatch leading to false-positive divergence alerts
Customer confusion if opt-in UX not clear about enforcement semantics
rollback_plan: Primary rollback: flip canary cluster flag to disable v2 enforcement and stop writes to v2 enforcement index; trigger reconciliation job with high priority to merge fixes back to v1 if any. Ops-runbook has scripted steps: 1) disable enforcement flag, 2) switch routing for read evaluation to v1 (3min target), 3) run divergence sampler and publish report. Secondary rollback: global feature-flag kill-switch and DB-level write-block if automated rollback fails.
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: divergence_rate > 0.1% sustained for 6 hours => P1 oncall
Alert: backfill_write_errors > 0.5% per minute => auto-throttle backfill and page ops
Dashboard: canary/org-level heatmap with per-org divergence, top failing principals, recent SAML mapping errors
communications: Customer-facing: 2-week opt-in window email + Console banner explaining shadow vs enforcement
Internal: Slack #rbac-migrations daily updates during canary weeks, weekly engineering sync with PM and Security
Support runbook: FAQ for customers about access regressions and how to opt-out quickly
